Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight.

AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load.

The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production.

Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads.

With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

items.excerpt:
The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.

Since 1991, U.S. refinery utilization has averaged 92% from May to September, compared with 88% across the other seven months.

U.S. refineries tend to run at their highest rates between May and September to boost supply of gasoline for the peak demand season in the summer months. Distillate demand, by contrast, peaks in the fall and winter. Because refineries produce a combination of gasoline and distillates, high summer refinery utilization usually leads to an increase in distillate inventories before seasonal refinery maintenance and the peak distillate demand season.

This year the refinery runs were driven largely by tight global supplies for distillate fuel oil, leading to high international demand for U.S. distillate fuel oil exports.

While refinery utilization was the highest since 1998, total U.S. refinery output was only the highest since 2019 because refining capacity has decreased by 4% since then.

In the first 3 weeks of October, U.S. refinery utilization decreased from its summer highs but remained above the five-year (2021–2025) seasonal average.

Every decade or so, a shift in software forces us to rethink computer architecture from first principles. After the first boom of web-scale traffic, Google pioneered warehouse-scale computing and Linux containers on Borg. This reshaped how we run internal workloads and ultimately sparked the modern cloud-native ecosystem through Kubernetes. A decade later, when deep learning models outgrew their compute and power needs, we went back to the drawing board and created Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). And as cloud security demanded stronger, hardware-rooted guarantees, we built Titanium, a custom silicon and Infrastructure Processing Unit (IPU) architecture that offloads I/O virtualization, storage, and cryptographic trust from the host CPU.

Today, we are in the middle of the next foundational shift: the transition to agentic AI that goes beyond answering questions and to taking action.

Across Google, AI agents are writing and executing code, running tools, driving browsers, orchestrating enterprise workflows, and iterating on software repositories. In a remarkably short span of time, agentic workloads have grown into one of the fastest-expanding consumers of compute and storage across our fleet.

Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant.

NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost.

Gemini — your helpful AI assistant — is now available globally on Android Auto and cars with Google built-in. With Gemini, you can speak naturally to get more done or brainstorm ideas while driving.

An assistant is even more helpful when it knows the world and knows you. That’s why we’re rolling out Personal Intelligence with Gemini starting today, 1 to give you uniquely tailored answers and make Gemini even more valuable on the road.

With your permission, Personal Intelligence securely connects information from the Google apps you already use — Workspace (including Gmail and Google Calendar), Google Photos, Google Maps, YouTube, and Search.

Personal Intelligence has two core strengths: retrieving specific details from, say, an email, photo or a place you saved in Google Maps to answer your question and reasoning across complex sources. That’s especially helpful when your hands are on the wheel. Personal Intelligence does the heavy lifting so you can speak naturally, without having to explain context or dig for information. items.excerpt:
National security agencies and other sovereign and highly regulated organizations handle incredibly sensitive data such as classified reports, field manuals, and sensitive multi-modal datasets. Search and multimodal intelligence that’s available in the public cloud can help teams manage and analyze that data, but due to strict data sovereignty mandates, that data cannot leave the customer premises.

The alternative has been to deploy custom agentic search inside a secure, disconnected perimeter, but until now, that meant months building and maintaining custom infrastructure — stitching together models, building speech-to-text and optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines, configuring vector databases, and managing a bespoke user interface.

Today, we're excited to announce enterprise search capabilities with Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped accelerated by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to help solve the above challenges. In preview, this fully managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search experience runs entirely inside your physical security perimeter, with no connection to the public internet or to Google Cloud's global infrastructure. Your teams can now upload their files into a conversation and ask Gemini to find information about it, summarize it, compare it, or translate it. Every answer cites its sources, and conversations persist between sessions.
